prompt_md: A 100 kg sack of potatoes is 99% water. Left out to dry, the potatoes lose water until they're 98% water. How many kilograms do they weigh now?
prompt_short: 100 kg of potatoes, 99% water, dry to 98% water. New weight?
hint_md: The dry part doesn't change. How much is there?
explain_intuition_md: Only 1 kg of the sack is not water, and drying doesn't touch it. At 98% water, that same 1 kg has to be 2% of the total, so the sack must weigh 50 kg.
explain_math_md: Dry matter $= 1$ kg $= 2\%$ of the new weight $w$, so $w = \frac{1}{0.02} = 50$ kg.
